title: workflow
description: Workflow definition file; its activities are the files in its activities/ folder and the files it references.

$schema.description: URI of the JSON Schema for this workflow definition.

activity.description: Rules for the workers executing each activity.

items.description: Rule for both the orchestrator and activity workers.

universal.description: Rules for both the orchestrator and activity workers.

rules.description: Rules grouped by audience: workflow orchestrator, activity workers, or both.

anyOf.description: Qualified snake_case noun phrase of at least two words: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters and digits, with each further word after a single underscore (`analysis_target`, never bare `target`).

name.description: Snake_case noun phrase of at least two words, or a listed single-word exemption.

type.description: Declared variable type. A value written to the session, through a checkpoint `setVariable` effect or a reported variable change, is checked against it; a mismatch is stored as written with a warning, and a `{name}` template value is exempt.

description.description: Meaning and intended use of the variable.

items.description: Allowed string value for the variable.

values.description: Complete set of values the variable admits: nonempty, without repeats, and declared only on a `string` variable. A declared `defaultValue` must be one of them. A value written outside the set is stored as written with a warning, and a `{name}` template value is exempt.

defaultValue.description: Initial value, present from the start of every session and child session. Do not gate a defaulted variable with `exists` or `notExists`: the variable is always present, so the gate is constant, and `check:variable-model` rejects it.

required.description: Marks the variable as expected to be set; no check reads it.

items.description: Variable declaration with type, allowed values, and an optional initial value.

variables.description: Declarations of the session facts and policy this workflow file owns, spanning activities. A variable an activity writes is declared in that activity's `variables.writes` and contributed here when the activity joins the graph. Declarations of one name that each name a different type, starting value or value set fail the load; one silent about a starting value takes the value another names.

workflow.description: Technique references for workflow orchestration, using `::`-separated paths.

items.description: Technique reference shared by every activity.

activity.description: Technique references that apply to every activity.

techniques.description: Technique references grouped by scope: workflow orchestration or every activity.

initialActivity.description: Identifier of the first activity to execute: the activity the first `next_activity` names, and the root the variable-reachability analysis walks from. Naming no activity of this workflow fails the load.

anyOf.description: Destination activity identifier, or `__terminal__` to end the workflow.
Identifier of an activity to run once.

activity.description: Activity every instance runs; instances differ only by the element each receives.

over.description: Collection the activity runs once per element of: a variable name or a dotted path into one (`work_units`, `execution_plan.steps`). Read when the fan is entered, so its length then is the fan's width. The fan is refused unless the collection is present, an array, and nonempty, with each element a string or an object carrying a string `id`, and no two elements sharing an id.

variable.description: Variable name each instance reads its own element at, declared among the names the activity `reads`. Name it as the consuming technique's input identifier so no step needs a rename.

maxInstances.description: Widest fan this destination admits, at least two, narrowing the server's configured ceiling. A fan wider than either bound is refused when entered, naming the bound that applied and the width it saw.

anyOf.description: Activity repeated in parallel for each element of a collection.

items.description: One fan member: an activity identifier to run once, or an instance fan. A member is never itself a list, so fans do not nest.

anyOf.description: Two or more members run together, one worker each. Every exit of every branch names the same single activity, the join, which the run enters once, after the last branch returns.

additionalProperties.description: Next activity, terminal outcome, or parallel group of activities or collection instances.
Exit identifiers mapped to destinations for one activity.

graph.description: Activity identifiers mapped to exit identifiers and their destinations. A destination is one of: an activity identifier, which the run enters next; `__terminal__`, which ends the run; a list of two or more members, each an activity identifier or an instance fan, run together with one worker each; or a single instance fan, which runs one activity once per element of a collection. A fan's width is the number of branches once every member is flattened, an instance fan counting its collection's length when entered; it is bounded by the server's ceiling and by any `maxInstances` an instance fan declares. Every exit of every branch names the fan's join, one single activity, and the load fails otherwise, so a branch cannot open a fan of its own; the run enters the join once, after the last branch returns. Each fanned activity's outputs land in an array variable named for it, its id with `-` replaced by `_` and `_outputs` appended (`review-unit` lands in `review_unit_outputs`), one slot per branch in collection order, each carrying its unit's id and that branch's values. Every exit of every activity is bound here: an unbound exit, an unknown exit and an unknown destination each fail the load. Omitted only when no activity declares exits.

items.description: Activity file reference. `<NN>-<id>.yaml` names a file in this workflow's own `activities/` folder; `<workflow>/[activities/][<folder>/…]<NN>-<id>.yaml` names a file under that workflow's `activities/` folder, subfolders included, such as `work-package/02-design-philosophy.yaml` or `meta/patterns/02-supervisor.yaml`.

activities.description: Activities referenced by file, beyond the files in this workflow's `activities/` folder; a reference to another workflow's activity borrows it.

workflow.description: Workflow definition file: identity, shared declarations, activity references, and exit destinations.
